bar.note: iA publishes no latency numbers (only 'boots in a whizz… snappy as jazz'). Bar = best native editors: Sublime 32.5 ms / TextEdit 33.4 ms keyboard-to-photon (Tristan Hume, macOS); internal input→paint ≤5 ms (Typometer, Notepad++ 4.3 ms). Sources in ref/ia/REFERENCE.md.

pieces.title: The page
pieces.judge: the page itself: paper colour, margins, the measure (line length), vertical placement of text in the window, scrolling feel implied by spacing, how the empty space frames the text; overall calm. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: The type
pieces.what: Duo / Quattro / Mono, size, line height, rhythm
pieces.judge: the typography only: typeface rendering, size, line height, rhythm, weight and colour of the ink, the spacing of blank lines, how italic/bold sit; would a writer rather read and type in this type. Text size and line pitch are set by a published fourteen-step ladder, one pitch per step (docs/design.md, rows Text sizes and Line pitch), so the gap to name is a pitch or a size that misses its own step, not a pitch you would have set differently. Where a state is a crop of the text column rather than a whole window, judge the type inside the crop. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Cursor & caret
pieces.judge: the caret and selection only: caret colour, width, height relative to the line, how it sits against the glyphs, blink/motion implied, selection colour; does the caret feel like a precise, alive instrument. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. Nor is how far a selection reaches: docs/design.md rows Selection, Held newline and Multi-row fill make a selection a fill of the text container, so a row the selection runs past is filled to the container's right edge and a row it entered from above starts at the container's left, gutter and all, and only the anchor and the focus are measured off glyphs — a band wider than the words beneath it is that rule and not a gap

pieces.title: Focus & typewriter
pieces.judge: focus mode and typewriter scrolling: how the non-focused text is dimmed (colour, amount), sentence vs paragraph scope, where the active line rests in the window, whether the eye is drawn to exactly the right place. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Dark & light
pieces.judge: the two palettes: paper and ink colours, contrast, how the markers read against the words, whether the ground feels designed rather than inverted. Both states are a crop of the Design oracle at a passage carrying every mark kind, so what is in front of you is the page itself and none of the furniture around it: judge the paper, the ink on it, and how the `>`, the `-`, the `1.` and the task box sit against the words they mark. A marker that reads as loud as its words is the answer here rather than a defect — the Design oracle rests every mark kind at the body's own ink (docs/design.md row Markers), and a quieted marker on either side is the gap

pieces.title: Markup rendering
pieces.what: Headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code, links in the editor
pieces.judge: how Markdown is shown while writing: heading markers, emphasis, lists, blockquotes, code, links — are markers quiet, does the text stay readable, do headings and structure read at a glance without the text jumping. Both states are the hanging-marker gutter and the body column: gutters is the six heading levels, whose `#` runs step out into the left gutter by level + 1 cells so their words all land on the body column and `###### ` reaches the container's own left edge; blocks is that deepest heading above a quote, a bullet and an ordinal, none of which hangs — `>`, `-` and `1.` sit on the body column and push their own words inward, and no rule is drawn beside a quote. Judge where each row starts and how the two columns read together. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Chrome & menus
pieces.what: Bars, counters, palette, what hides while typing, the empty state
pieces.judge: the chrome: what UI is visible around the text, the stats/word-count bar, title, menus/palette, how it recedes while writing; is there exactly as much interface as a writer needs and no more. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: File handling
pieces.judge: file handling UI: the library/sidebar, file list, how documents are named and found, open/save affordances, how it looks next to the editor; would a writer trust it with their manuscripts. log.msg: Harness up: headless Chromium screenshots, latency bench, blind A/B pairing. Core editor engine written (textarea + mirror, incremental line render, custom caret, focus/typewriter, markdown tokenizer).

Reference package in: 49 real iA Writer screenshots (App Store, MS Store, ia.net) with verbatim transcriptions, Duo/Quattro/Mono fonts (OFL) with parsed metrics, measured spec sheet (paper #f9f9f9 / #1a1a1a, ink #1c1c1c / #cccccc, caret #00b5ff ≈0.15 em wide, line pitch ≈1.7×, 64-char measure, hanging # markers), latency bar from third-party measurements.

All nine pieces picked blind. Latency won on round 4: app-internal 2.43 ms mean / 15.61 ms worst (bar ≤5/≤16), real keys via /dev/uinput → presented frame 12.17 ms, caret settles 8.1 ms after the key (was 57 ms), cold launch to first document frame 370 ms. Final integration smoke passed in all three fonts and both themes.
